title: UI wave 2 U6: Toolbar label mode and a labelled More menu (D)
description: Plan task U6. Follow docs/agent-work/2026-10-26-ui-wave-2/PLAN.md exactly: this task's section (Files, Interfaces, Steps, Acceptance check, Fail-first, Stop-and-ask, Default) plus the seven answered Open questions and the Notes for the implementer. Protocol: register the serial check slot via files add only right before the first expensive check and keep it until done; pinned Node; quoted --outDir; no installs, no commits; status CLAIMED; independent review required.

review.note: APPROVED T103 (U6), reviewer agent-1054. Own build (ui2-u6-review/dist): tsc --noEmit clean; Playwright editor-toolbar + motion-u6 + accessibility = 14 passed. Re-measured myself (viewport -> bar): 1280 icons 10 groups on bar (3 more-groups in More), 1300 icons 11, 1100 icons 8; 1440 labels 6 on bar; 1920 labels 7. Sweep 1600/1400/1380/1370/1360/1100/1390/2200/900/1600: data-labels flips exactly at bar 1100, scrollWidth == clientWidth every time, refit correct both directions. More at 1440: 19 rows, all with data-popover-item, shortcut right-aligned and muted, labels aria-hidden, aria-labels unchanged; at 850x600 the menu is capped (clientHeight 481 of 686) and scrolls, bottom 598 < 600. Screenshots viewed (more-1440, more-850). Native: existing smoke debug binary (built 02:44, after all T103 files last changed) run via scripts/native-smoke.py: phase 1 passed including step 'native WebKit page fragmentation and continuous toggle' with pageViewToggle=overflowed at 1240x812, i.e. Page view found inside More and clicked. Phase 3 database check later failed (expected 'Acknowledged SQLite checkpoint.' found 'Journaled recovery after deliberate kill.') in the recovery/kill phase; unrelated to the toolbar, but my run overlapped T105's slot use (I checked the owner too late), so treat as possibly collision-caused. Weakness (not blocking): motion-u6 passes on the old tree too. OWNER DECISION (open question 3): at a 1440 px window the bar is 1170 px in label mode: only Undo/Redo, zoom, paragraph style, font, More, Comment/Keep-as-fragment fit; Bold, sizes, link, insert, lists, indent, view, aids are all in More (over half the groups). Shipped per plan; threshold LABEL_MIN_WIDTH is one constant.

MEASUREMENTS (viewport = bar + 270 sidebar; 'n of 13' = overflowable groups on the bar, rest in More; raw: ui2-u6/measure-sweep.txt). ICON mode: bar 730: 4; 830: 5; 880-930: 6; 980: 7 (lists); 1010: Insert image/table/Table controls still in More (U3 gap effect confirmed at viewport 1280); 1030-1090: 8 (+insert, inline from bar ~1030 = viewport ~1300); 1099: 9 (+indent). LABEL mode: bar 1100: 3 (zoom, paragraph, font) -- 10 of 13 in More; 1170 (viewport 1440): 3; 1330 (1600): 4; 1430: 4; 1650 (1920): 4; 1830-2130: 6 (+marks, link); 2230: 7 (+lists); 2530: 8 (+insert). Cliff: 9 groups at bar 1099 vs 3 at 1100. So at a 1440 px viewport more than half the groups are in More (the plan's stop-and-ask case); open question 3 says ship as decided and record, so shipped. Owner option: shorter labels (e.g. Smaller/Larger) or a threshold of about 1600-1900 would keep most groups on the bar. Gap token unchanged.
SCREENSHOTS viewed (ui2-u6/shots): bar at 2200 and 1440 (labels), 1100 (icons), More at 1440 (labels) and 850 (icons), light and dark: labelled rows, muted shortcut right, sliding highlight on hovered row. Shots predate the scroll fix; 850 More is now height-capped and scrolls (accessibility tests reach Page view).
DESIGN DOC: Toolbar -- the format bar shows a 12 px label beside every icon when its width is >= 1100 px (data-labels on .format-bar); below that icons only. Overflowing groups move into More in OVERFLOW_ORDER in both modes; widths are cached per mode and the bar re-measures on crossing 1100. More is a vertical list of labelled rows (var(--control-height)) with the muted shortcut right-aligned and one sliding highlight (Popover highlight=follow; rows carry data-popover-item); it scrolls when taller than the window. Labels are aria-hidden: the accessible name stays the aria-label (e.g. "Bold (⌘B)").
